content.title: About
content.content: Beef tenderloin is a lean cut taken from the spine of the cattle. A raw tenderloin steak is known for its buttery texture and mild flavor, with very little connective tissue or fat. It is commonly used for quick grilling or pan‑searing.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tenderloin is the most expensive and prized cut of beef because of its tenderness.
Raw tenderloin steak is a classic base for steak tartare and carpaccio.
The meat is rich in creatine, which supports muscle energy metabolism.
Tenderloin contains less intramuscular fat than ribeye or strip steak, making it lower in calories.
When stored properly, raw tenderloin can stay fresh in the fridge for up to 2 days.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 g of complete protein, essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tenderloin contains less than 5 g of fat per 100 g, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron and zinc, which support immune function and blood formation.

items.title: Vitamin B12 source
items.content: Provides vitamin B12, important for nerve health and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Contains creatine
items.content: Creatine helps improve physical performance and muscle strength.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Raw beef can harbor pathogenic bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella; proper cooking is essential.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: People with gout or elevated uric acid should limit intake.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may react to beef proteins.

items.title: Sodium in processed versions
items.content: If the steak is marinated or cured, sodium levels can be high.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw tenderloin steak is typically seared quickly over high heat to the desired doneness (rare‑medium). It can be sliced thin for salads, used in steak tartare, or quickly stir‑fried in a wok.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw tenderloin in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at +1‑+4 °C for no more than 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C in a vacuum‑sealed bag. Discard if it develops an off‑odor.
